prior_hypothesis_status: RESOLVED at repair 116 (DEF-W57-017 closed and verified end to end). It is NOT re-tested here and is NOT reused: an identical rerun of it would be a no-progress cycle.
finding: Repair 116 closed with the claim that 'no W57-owned repair action remains' and that the only outstanding items are the external compute02 outage and a controller-owned materialization obligation. That claim is incomplete. The Wave's own canonical report, section 6, still carries owned row HPC-W10-TODO-011 at PARTIAL for exactly one reason: 'the LOCAL_PASSWORD_REAL password leg was not re-executed this run and no prior leg is reusable against the new candidate'. That is a W57-owned acceptance gap, it is the only owned row left PARTIAL, and it is neither gated by the compute02 outage nor owned by the controller. It was never attempted.
observed_failure: HPC-W10-TODO-011 is an owned ACTIVE row whose text is 'Real local OpenSSH password/key/host-key acceptance'. Of its three mechanisms, key and host-key were already proven live against LOCAL_REAL (login-control01 and compute01 over real SSH; host keys pinned on all three nodes at repair 116). The password mechanism had NO real evidence at all: the only harness in the repository that exercises password authentication, scripts/wx_packaged_smoke.py, drives it through an in-process mock (support.mock_ssh_server.MockSSHServer, via HPC_GUI_PACKAGED_SMOKE_SSH_PASSWORD). LOCAL_REAL_HYPERV is key-only (ssh_pwauth: false) and the project protocol states it 'must not be used as password-auth evidence'. The designated real password target, LOCAL_PASSWORD_REAL, was not running: 127.0.0.1:2222 was not listening and no hpclab container existed.
hypothesis: The password leg of HPC-W10-TODO-011 was left unclosed not because it was unexecutable but because it was never attempted. LOCAL_PASSWORD_REAL is a maintained, documented Docker fixture (devtools/lab/docker-compose.yml) bound to 127.0.0.1:2222, so it needs neither the downed compute02 guest nor an elevated Hyper-V operator. Tested by bringing that maintained fixture up with its own maintained command and executing real password acceptance, plus the negative invalid-password case, against the exact frozen candidate.
change: NO product, test, spec, build-input, candidate or security change. The frozen candidate was neither patched nor rebuilt and still hashes to 8BA80453... . The only repository writes by this phase are this W57-owned evidence artifact and the W57 canonical report section recording the result. The fixture was created by the documented maintained lifecycle command and is disposable state under .tmp/.
result: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. HPC-W10-TODO-011 moves off PARTIAL: the password leg now has real, non-mock, correctly negative-paired acceptance against a real OpenSSH server, executed by the frozen candidate itself. The predecessor's 'no W57-owned repair action remains' is falsified.

positive_case_real_password_acceptance.password_delivery: stdin redirect from a .tmp file; never on the command line, never in argv, never in this artifact or in the Wave report
positive_case_real_password_acceptance.interpretation: The frozen candidate performed a genuine password-authenticated SSH session, SFTP subsystem init and Slurm session against a real OpenSSH/Slurm server. The auth stage is the acceptance subject; the sftp/slurm/checksum stages are recorded as proof the target is real infrastructure and are NOT claimed as LOCAL_PASSWORD_REAL evidence, which the protocol scopes to password only.

negative_case_invalid_password_rejection.command: identical, with a deliberately wrong password (a freshly generated random GUID, not the fixture value and not any real secret)
negative_case_invalid_password_rejection.why_this_leg_exists: A positive result alone cannot distinguish real authentication from a bypassed or skipped auth path. The paired negative proves the server genuinely enforced the credential, that the product reported the failure truthfully and visibly, and that it did not fall back to any other mechanism. This is the invalid-password rejection the protocol names as the second half of this target's authority.
